item.title: A Stop On The Underground Railroad Has Been Discovered Hidden Inside New York’s Historic Merchant’s House
item.description: The Merchant's House Museum in Manhattan was built by abolitionist Joseph Brewster in 1832 — and a secret passage behind its walls now appears to have been a stop on the Underground Railroad. item.description: Genghis Khan is believed to have had so many children that some 16 million men alive today are directly descended from the Mongol emperor. The post The Story Of Genghis Khan’s Children And The Staggering Spread Of His DNA Around The World appeared first on All That's Interesting.

item.title: The Grisly Glasgow Smile, The Torture Method Devised By Scottish Gangs
item.description: In 20th-century Scotland, roving gangsters punished each other by carving the sides of a victim's mouth into a demented grin known as the "Glasgow smile." But this bloody practice didn't end there. The post The Grisly Glasgow Smile, The Torture Method Devised By Scottish Gangs appeared first on All That's Interesting.

item.title: Archaeologists Have Uncovered A Siberian Ice Mummy Who Underwent Jaw Surgery 2,500 Years Ago
item.description: Members of the ancient Pazyryk culture of Central Asia drilled two holes in a woman's injured jawbone and threaded it together with hair or tendon to create a "primitive prosthetic" circa 500 B.C.E.
